notes: The interrogative particle and the negative are each written once in Hebrew and twice in English across the coordinated clauses; both occurrences belong to the one morpheme under rule 25, and the resuming הוּא is unrepresented because rule 20's fronted-copula sentence gives the single art to the particle.
is able is read as the existential frame of אֵין (rule 50); the competing reading gives able to the infinitive under rule 52 and is named in the unit's note.
בְּיָדְךָ is the clause's predicate and keeps the copula on the preposition, כֹּחַ being the subject (rule 49's closing paragraph).
